values.value: How much of your workflow logic depends on re-enrolment, goal criteria, or go-to-action steps that jump backwards — as opposed to a straight sequence of branches and delays?

[{"value":1,"label":"Re-enrolment is on across most workflows, goals drive exits, and at least one workflow loops backwards. The re-entry behaviour IS the programme."},{"value":2,"label":"Several workflows re-enrol or use goal criteria; removing them would change what the programme does. Maybe one backwards jump."},{"value":3,"label":"Mostly linear branch-and-delay logic; re-enrolment is on in a handful of places and is not load-bearing. No loops."},{"value":4,"label":"Linear, single-entry flows throughout. No goals, no loops, no re-enrolment anywhere."}]

Ask them to open one workflow and read out its enrolment settings — 're-enrol contacts' and 'goal' are checkboxes, so this is a factual answer rather than an impression. Then ask whether any workflow has a go-to-action step, and where it points.
If you are not sure, open one of your busier workflows: 're-enrol contacts' and 'goal' are checkboxes in its settings, and a go-to-action step is visible on the canvas.

capabilities/platforms/sfmc.yaml — flow_control.loops unsupported, "Journey Builder does not support loopbacks - contacts only move forward", and gap_patterns loopback_flow at blocker. migration-accelerator/capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml — the three source-side patterns this question is anchored on and their CLASSIC severities, which are not the MCN ones: workflow_loop_go_to_action is "Blocker for both classic SFMC and SFMC Next — the constraint is identical", while workflow_reenrollment and workflow_goal_criteria are major, with classic SFMC's stated approximations being a re-entry-enabled journey plus a scheduled Automation Studio query, and journey Exit Criteria, respectively. That asymmetry is why the anchors put the LOOP at option 1 and let re-enrolment alone sit at 2-3: on this target a loop is a redesign and re-enrolment is a scheduled query, and an anchor set that scored them alike would be reporting a rebuild where there is a build.
